test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 06 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: If the selling price of a bed is 2-times of initial, then the profit is 11-times of initial. Find the initial profit percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial **Profit** be P and initial **Selling Price** be SP.

New Profit = 11 × P and New SP = 2 × SP.

Since **Cost Price (CP)** is constant, Change in Profit = Change in SP.

(11P − P) = (2SP − SP) ⇒ 10P = 1SP.

Ratio of P : SP = 1 : 10. Since SP = CP + P, then CP = 10 − 1 = 9.

Initial Profit% = (P ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 9) × 100 = 11 1/9 %.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 1/9 %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → New SP = 2 × Old SP | New Profit = 11 × Old Profit.
Formulas: Profit = SP − CP | Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b1536861bd094cef7e087c3e6b65f5c368c0c4707aab0279d9893c8ea237489.png] 
⇒ Let initial CP be **x** and initial SP be **y**.
⇒ Initial Profit (P) = y − x.
⇒ New SP = 2y. New Profit = 2y − x.
⇒ According to the question: 2y − x = 11(y − x).
⇒ 2y − x = 11y − 11x ⇒ 10x = 9y ⇒ y/x = 10/9.
⇒ If CP = 9 units, SP = 10 units. Profit = 1 unit.
⇒ Profit% = (1 ÷ 9) × 100 = 11 1/9 %.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 1/9 %.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relationship between SP and Profit

When the cost price remains **constant**, any increase in the selling price directly increases the profit by the same absolute amount.

Profit Percentage

Profit percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)** unless stated otherwise. Formula: [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.</p
